title: Marguerite de La Tullaye
text:
Gérer l’environnement virtuel sous Linux :
D’abord, créer l’environnement virtuel :
sudo apt install python3-pip python3-venv
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
Puis, y installer quarto :
pip install quarto-cli
quarto --version

title: Marguerite de La Tullaye
text:
Work with Quarto
Quarto has to be set up on the computer through : 1. Quarto installation (in my Program\ files) through the website : https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/ 2. the VScode Quarto installation to have files with the .yml extension colored fancyfully
To verify Quarto is well installed, run quarto --version in Bash. \
Then, to have a local preview of the website :
quarto preview
It opens at http://localhost:xxxx with live reload. Type Ctrl + C to close the localhost.
To deploy :
quarto render
git add -A
git commit -m "update site"
git push
GitHub Pages is configured to serve from the main branch, /docs folder. If it is not, turn it on GitHub Pages. On GitHub : * Settings → Pages (menu gauche) * Source → Deploy from a branch * Branch → main / docs * Click Save

title: Marguerite de La Tullaye
text:
HTML files — the pages themselves
Without Quarto, the repository would be organised as follows:



File / Folder


Sub-element


Description




index.html


Mandatory entry point. When someone visits yourusername.github.io, the server automatically looks for a file named index.html at the root. It is your homepage — every website needs one.




assets/


css/style.css


Controls the visual appearance — colors, fonts, spacing, layout, and animations. Linked in the <head> of each HTML file.




js/main.js


Adds interactivity — dropdown menus, form validation, scroll animations, or API calls. Loaded just before </body>.




img/


Stores images and other media. Keeping them in a dedicated folder prevents clutter.



The assets/ folder holds all the supporting files your HTML pages depend on. The name is a convention — static/ or public/ would work equally well.

I chose to deploy this website through Quarto, which makes it easier to integrate mathematical equations. The reference file uses the .qmd suffix instead of .html, and the repository is structured as follows:



File / Folder


Description




_quarto.yml


Defines the site structure, navigation, and external links.




index.qmd, cv.qmd, research.qmd


Root-level files encoding the main pages of the site.




assets/css/custom.scss


Controls the visual design of the site. The assets/ folder can hold additional resources if needed.




assets/img/


Stores images used across the site.




fr/


Contains the French version of the site, mirroring the root structure.




docs/.nojekyll


Tells GitHub Pages not to run Jekyll on docs/. Required for Quarto sites, as Jekyll would otherwise ignore folders starting with _.
